name: Safety Reports at Release
summary: The lab publishes a system card with dangerous-capability and alignment results for each frontier model, at or before its release.
description: A system card is the main public evidence of how a lab tested a model. A late or missing card means that people use the model before anyone outside the lab can check its risks.

criteria.label: Every Frontier Release
criteria.description: Each frontier model release gets a card, also updates that add much capability.

criteria.label: At Release
criteria.description: The card comes out at or before the release, not weeks after it.

criteria.label: Dangerous Capabilities
criteria.description: The card gives results of evaluations for biological, chemical, cyber and autonomy risks.

criteria.label: Alignment
criteria.description: The card gives results of alignment and misbehavior evaluations.

criteria.label: Outside Testers
criteria.description: The card names the outside testers and tells what they found.

orgs.summary: OpenAI publishes system cards at launch under SB 53, with named outside testers; GPT-5.4 Pro shipped without its own card in March 2026.

events.title: Signs White House pledge to publish model reports
events.summary: Joins the White House voluntary commitments. Signers say they will publish reports for all new significant public model releases in scope, with safety evaluations and adversarial testing results.

sources.title: Ensuring Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI

events.title: Framework promises Preparedness results for major deployments
events.summary: Version 2 of the Preparedness Framework says OpenAI will release information about its Preparedness Framework results for major deployments. The information can be redacted or summarized.

quote.text: We will release information about our Preparedness Framework results in order to facilitate public awareness of the state of frontier AI capabilities for major deployments.

events.title: GPT-4.1 ships without a safety report
events.summary: TechCrunch reports that GPT-4.1 launched with no system card. OpenAI says GPT-4.1 is not a frontier model, so it gets no separate card.

sources.title: OpenAI ships GPT-4.1 without a safety report

events.title: California law requires transparency reports at deployment
events.summary: California's SB 53 takes effect. Large frontier developers must publish risk assessment summaries before or at deployment. OpenAI's May 2026 framework says it publishes assessment details in system cards at launch.

quote.text: We also publish details of these assessments in system cards or in other reporting when a model launches.

sources.title: SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers.

events.title: Astra card names five outside evaluators
events.summary: The GPT-6 Astra system card, published at launch, reports Critical cyber capability. It names UK AISI, Apollo Research, SecureBio, Gray Swan and Irregular as outside evaluators.

events.title: Outside evaluators publish their own Astra reports
events.summary: SecureBio publishes its own pre-release assessment of Astra's biology capabilities. UK AISI publishes a report on Astra's unsanctioned supply-chain attacks in simulated cyber tests.

sources.title: Evaluating Whether GPT-6 Astra Performs Unsanctioned Supply-Chain Attacks
Pre-Release Assessment of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra

events.title: Muse Spark 1.3 report follows 51 days after release

events.title: Publishes Inkling card with safety section at launch
events.summary: The Inkling model card and launch post, out on release day, describe CBRN, cyber, loss-of-control and misuse testing. They give refusal benchmark scores and say outside testers checked the results.

quote.text: We trained Inkling to an internal spec of safe model behavior across all modalities. We then commissioned external safety testers to verify the results.

events.title: Names four outside testers and calls testing necessary
events.summary: A Safe Path to Open Weights says safety testing must be part of each model release. It names Scale AI, Handshake AI, FAR.AI and Apollo Research as Inkling's outside testers and sums up their findings.

quote.text: Robust safety testing – an imperfect but essential proxy for real-world capability in dangerous domains – must be a necessary part of our model release process.

sources.title: A Safe Path to Open Weights

events.title: Inkling 2 Small post gives cyber and alignment results

quote.text: We intend to make the full weights available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.
